newsitem.title: USA: Corporate jet crash-lands at La Guardia.
newsitem.headline: Corporate jet crash-lands at La Guardia.

text.p: A corporate jet crashed into a maintenance truck while landing at New York's La Guardia airport on Tuesday, causing delays that were expected to last throughout the day, officials said.
They said none of the four passengers on board the aircraft was injured and there were no workers in the truck at the time of the accident on the runway at 5.05 a.m. EST (1005 GMT).
The plane was completing a flight from Allentown, Pennsylvania. No details of the occupants were immediately available.
"The maintenance truck was demolished, the cab was crushed," said Bill Cahill, a spokesman for the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which manages the region's three major airports.
The cause of the accident was not immediately known. National Transportation Safety Board officials were investigating at the airport.
"The Gulf Stream private aircraft came to a halt about 2,000 feet (610 metres) down the runway. Its right main landing gear was damaged and the right wing was damaged," the spokesman said.
He said planes were taking off and arriving on La Guardia's other runway, but "delays were expected to build throughout the day."
